headline: AI stock rout after the Democratic sweep: yen holds, Aussie and won sink, dollar flat
summary: The dollar index ended roughly flat near 101.5 after dipping to about 101.2, its lowest since Sept 30, as a haven bid during a 4.4% S&P 500 slide offset a drop in the two-year Treasury yield of about 11bp. The yen gained about 0.5% and the peso and ringgit rallied on local news, while the Aussie fell about 1.1% and the won and Taiwan dollar slid as foreigners dumped Asian chip stocks.
drivers: AI stocks crash after the Democratic sweep

Fears that a Democratic Congress will slow the AI data-centre buildout sent the Nasdaq down 5.5% and the chip index down about 12%, after foreigners sold a record 3.4tn won of Korean and NT$102bn of Taiwan shares. The yen, seen as the best hedge against AI selloffs, firmed to about 157.6, while the Aussie was the weakest G10 currency.
Fed hike pushed back, BoE hikes

Two-year US yields fell about 11bp and markets moved the next Fed hike to March, though jobless claims fell to 189,000, a 57-year low. The BoE raised rates to 4% on an 8–1 vote, with Mann wanting 50bp, but the pound slipped about 0.15% because markets already price about 100bp of hikes.

Philippine inflation jumped to 7.8%, above the 7.6% forecast, raising BSP hike bets and lifting the peso 0.9% to 62.97. Bank Negara held at 2.75% and the ringgit firmed to 4.0445, while Indonesian Q3 growth of 5.47%, above 5.2% expected, lifted the rupiah to 18,082.
view: Neutral overall, but split by currency for the next 1–2 weeks: lower US yields cap the dollar against the yen and franc, while the AI rout keeps it bid against the Aussie, won and Taiwan dollar. I sell dollar rallies against the yen near 158.20–158.50 and buy it on dips against the won and Taiwan dollar. A strong payrolls report that lifts the DXY above 102.20 would make me bullish; a close below 101.00 would turn me bearish across the board.
ideas: Sell 158.20–158.50 as the yen trades as the AI-selloff hedge and BoJ minutes stay hawkish; for 156.50, stop 159.40.
Sell 0.6970–0.6990 now that the 0.6950 floor broke and the RBA looks done; for 0.6850, stop 0.7050.
Buy 1,350–1,353 as record foreign selling of Korean chip stocks broke the 1,355 cap; for 1,375, stop 1,338.
review: Neither the USD/JPY sale at 158.80–159.20 nor the USD/TWD buy at 32.70–32.78 filled (the yen never got near 158.80 and the Taiwan dollar's best was 32.840) before both moved the called way, so I reset both entries. USD/CAD gave back its gain and I close the short at about its 1.4020 trailed stop; the ringgit sale is about 0.4% in favour and the rupiah long just held its 18,060 stop; AUD/USD, USD/KRW and USD/PHP broke their ranges, so those calls change.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.1% to near 1.1218 after a one-month high near 1.1270 in Asia; still mid-range.
eurusd.why: The dollar did the moving, both ways. It slid in Asia as the Democratic sweep pulled the 10-year Treasury yield to about 4.85%, lifting the euro to about 1.1261, then won back ground as the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and haven buying returned. Jobless claims at 189,000, below the 196,000 forecast, and Lagarde saying the ECB needs more data before December left the euro slightly lower.
eurusd.outlook: I keep the 1.1150–1.1300 range and buy dips: lower US yields help, but a risk-off dollar bid and a Fed still priced to hike cap rallies. A close above 1.1300 would open 1.1400; below 1.1150, I step aside.
eurusd.watch: US payrolls (Nov 6), ECB speakers, US-Iran talks and oil.

view.call: 1.1150–1.1300; buy dips, haven bid caps rallies.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.15% to near 1.3449 after the BoE hike; a six-day rally stalled below 1.3503.
gbpusd.why: Sterling did the moving after a hawkish hike that markets had already priced. The BoE raised rates to 4% on an 8–1 vote, with Mann wanting a half-point move, and Bailey said another hike is likely unless the Iran conflict eases, so two-year gilt yields rose about 4bp. But swaps already priced close to 100bp of tightening, so traders took profit and the pound ended slightly lower against a steadier dollar.
gbpusd.outlook: I keep the 1.3380–1.3560 range: rising gilt yields support dips, but heavy hike pricing and risk-off flows limit gains. A close above 1.3560 would open 1.3650.
gbpusd.watch: US payrolls (Nov 6), UK Q3 GDP, BoE speakers, BoE next decision (Dec 17).

view.call: 1.3380–1.3560; hawkish BoE, but hikes already priced.

audusd.note: Down about 1.1% to near 0.6929, the worst G10 performer; the 0.6950 range floor broke.
audusd.why: The Aussie did the moving as the market's favourite proxy for global risk and Asian tech. It slid as the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and chip stocks about 12%, with Korea's Kospi down 5.3% and Taiwan's Taiex down 3.2%. Rate support has also faded: the RBA's split 6–3 hike to 4.85% dropped its tightening bias, and Australia's 10-year yield fell to a 10-week low near 5.0%.
audusd.outlook: I turn bearish: the 0.6950–0.7060 range broke and the RBA looks done, so I sell rallies to 0.6970–0.6990 for 0.6850. A close above 0.7050 would end the call.
audusd.watch: US payrolls (Nov 6), China trade data, AI-stock sentiment, iron ore.

view.call: Sell 0.6970–0.6990; AI rout, RBA likely done.

usdjpy.note: Down about 0.5% to near 157.6 after a dip to about 157.4; the yen led as stocks fell.
usdjpy.why: The yen did the moving. Minutes of the BoJ's September meeting showed board members saw the need to keep hiking, with one open to a faster pace, and the yen then caught a haven bid as the Nasdaq fell 5.5%. Goldman notes the dollar tends to fall against the yen when the Nasdaq lags the S&P 500, and two-year Treasury yields fell about 11bp.
usdjpy.outlook: I keep selling rallies but lower the entry to 158.20–158.50 for 156.50: the yen is the hedge of choice in the AI unwind and the BoJ is leaning hawkish. A close above 159.40 would end the call.
usdjpy.watch: US payrolls (Nov 6), Japan wage data, Tokyo comments, BoJ speakers ahead of December.

view.call: Sell 158.20–158.50; yen is the AI hedge, BoJ hawkish.

usdchf.note: Little changed near 0.8160 after a dip toward 0.8130; still above the 0.8130 range floor.
usdchf.why: The franc held its haven gains rather than adding to them. Demand for safety rose with the 5.5% Nasdaq slide and a 1% rise in gold, but the dollar also caught a haven bid in New York. With Swiss inflation at 1.5%, the SNB has less reason to fight a strong franc, which keeps it near the lows.
usdchf.outlook: I keep the 0.8130–0.8280 range: haven flows favour the franc, but the SNB and crowded longs should slow it. A daily close below 0.8130 would open 0.8050.
usdchf.watch: Weekly sight deposits (Nov 9), US payrolls (Nov 6), equity sentiment.

usdcad.note: Up about 0.3% to near 1.4016 as the TSX fell 2%; the short is closed at about 1.4020.
usdcad.why: The loonie did the moving, giving back Wednesday's gains. Canadian stocks fell about 2% in the tech rout and the US dollar steadied, which outweighed a 3–4% rebound in oil to about $90.8 for WTI. Traders also squared positions before Friday's Canadian jobs report, after the loonie hit a seven-week high of 1.3927 on Wednesday.
usdcad.outlook: I close the short at about 1.4020 and move to a 1.3930–1.4080 range: cheaper oil and risk-off cap the loonie, while a soft US dollar caps the pair. A close below 1.3930 would reopen 1.3850.
usdcad.watch: Canada jobs and US payrolls (Nov 6), oil and US-Iran talks, BoC speakers.

usdcnh.note: Yuan firmer near 6.665 from 6.675 after a slightly stronger PBOC fixing at 6.7156.
usdcnh.why: Beijing eased off a little. The PBOC set the midpoint at 6.7156, slightly stronger than Wednesday's 6.7180 but still far weaker than the Reuters estimate of 6.6783, so it is still slowing the yuan's rise rather than reversing it. A 3.6% Hang Seng rally early on helped, and the yuan held up better than other Asian currencies when US stocks fell.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: the PBOC is slowing gains, but exporter conversion and a softer dollar limit any drop. A close above 6.70 would show Beijing wants more weakness.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, China trade data, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15).

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slows the yuan, dollar soft.

usdhkd.note: Little changed near 7.841, still near the weak end of the 7.75–7.85 band.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. One-month HIBOR eased to about 2.78% from 3.02% in late September, keeping the gap to US rates wide enough to favour selling Hong Kong dollars. A 3.6% Hang Seng rally in the day made little difference.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap holds it near 7.85, and only a sharp rise in HIBOR or HKMA buying would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Little changed near 1.2775, in the middle of its range after a dip to about 1.277.
usdsgd.why: The dollar's round trip set the tone. The Singapore dollar firmed to just over 1.277 in Asia as the dollar index hit a one-month low, then gave back a little as US stocks slumped. Gains were held back by heavy foreign selling of Korean and Taiwanese stocks, though the yuan's slightly stronger fixing helped.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2740–1.2860 range: the S$NEER's steady rise and a soft dollar favour the lower half, while regional outflows limit gains. A close below 1.2740 would open 1.2700.
usdsgd.watch: US payrolls (Nov 6), China trade data, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won closed at 1,342.1 in Seoul but fell to about 1,358 offshore as US chip stocks crashed.
usdkrw.why: The won did the moving. Foreigners sold a record net 3.4tn won of Kospi shares, a fifth straight day, as the index fell 5.28% on fears a Democratic Congress will slow AI spending; the sell-off in US chips later took the offshore rate through 1,355. Korean 10-year yields fell about 7.6bp to 3.89%, adding a little pressure.
usdkrw.outlook: I turn bullish: the 1,355 cap broke on record outflows, so I buy dips to 1,350–1,353 for 1,375. A close below 1,338 would end the call.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, US payrolls (Nov 6), AI-chip sentiment, authorities' comments.

view.call: Buy 1,350–1,353; record foreign selling of Kospi.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 5.5 cents to 32.876 in Taipei, then weakened past 33.0 offshore.
usdtwd.why: Equity outflows did the moving again. Foreigners sold a net NT$102.5bn of Taiwan shares, the 10th-largest day on record, as the Taiex fell 3.2% to its lowest since July 31 on AI data-centre worries. The Taiwan dollar has lost almost 40 cents this month, and the later 12% slide in US chip stocks pushed it past 33 offshore.
usdtwd.outlook: I stay long but reset the entry: buy dips to 32.85–32.95 for 33.30 while foreigners keep selling. A close below 32.65, or heavy central bank selling of dollars, would end the call.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, TSMC October sales (Nov 10), central bank smoothing, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: Buy 32.85–32.95; foreigners still selling Taiwan stocks.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit firmed to 4.0445/0490 at the 6pm close from 4.0610/0660 after Bank Negara held.
usdmyr.why: The ringgit did the moving. Bank Negara kept the OPR at 2.75% as expected and sounded upbeat on growth above 5%, while some economists see a hike in early 2027 because of inflation risks. That and a weaker dollar during Kuala Lumpur hours lifted the ringgit against the dollar and most regional peers.
usdmyr.outlook: I hold the sale, about 0.4% in favour, for 4.010 and trail the stop to 4.065: Bank Negara's steady stance supports the ringgit. A sharp regional risk-off move is the main threat.
usdmyr.watch: US payrolls (Nov 6), regional chip stocks, Malaysia trade data.

view.call: Short from 4.055–4.065; BNM steady, dollar soft.

usdphp.note: Peso jumped 56.5 centavos to 62.97, back below 63, after hotter October inflation.
usdphp.why: The peso did the moving. October inflation hit 7.8%, the highest since February 2023 and above the 7.6% forecast, with core at 5.4%, which strengthened bets on another BSP hike on Dec 17 after October's 50bp move to 5.5%. A broadly weaker dollar during Manila hours and Wednesday's 8.7% fall in Brent added support.
usdphp.outlook: I lower the range to 62.70–63.50: BSP hike bets and cheaper oil support the peso, but slowing growth and a regional risk-off limit gains. A close below 62.70 would open 62.30.
usdphp.watch: Philippine Q3 GDP, BSP comments, oil, US payrolls (Nov 6), BSP decision (Dec 17).

usdidr.note: Rupiah firmed 86 points to 18,082 after Q3 GDP of 5.47% beat the 5.2% forecast.
usdidr.why: The rupiah did the moving. Growth of 5.47% in the third quarter beat the 5.2% forecast, driven by government spending and domestic demand, and the weaker dollar helped the rupiah to its best levels since late October. It is still down about 8.3% this year on outflows and policy doubts.
usdidr.outlook: I keep the long for 18,300, now slightly against me, as the global tech rout should hit Asian assets on Friday; I would add at 18,100–18,130. A close below 18,060 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Bank Indonesia operations, foreign bond flows, US payrolls (Nov 6).

usdinr.note: Rupee firmed to 94.47 from 94.64, a fifth daily gain and a two-month high, after 94.32 intraday.
usdinr.why: The rupee gained on cheaper oil and foreign inflows. Brent's fall below $100 to about $94 cuts India's import bill, and foreigners bought about Rs 7,284 crore of Indian shares as India stood apart from the AI selloff. Oil companies and other importers bought dollars near 94.32, and the RBI is seen buying to rebuild reserves, which capped gains.
usdinr.outlook: I keep the 94.20–95.20 range: cheaper oil favours the rupee, but the RBI and importers buy dollars on dips. A Brent close back above $105 would push it toward 95.20.
usdinr.watch: Oil and US-Iran talks, RBI dollar buying, foreign flows, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 94.20–95.20; cheaper oil vs RBI dip buying.

eurjpy.note: Down about 0.6% to near 176.9 as the yen gained; back inside its range.
eurjpy.why: The yen did the moving. Hawkish BoJ minutes and a haven bid during the 5.5% Nasdaq slide lifted the yen, while the euro barely moved against the dollar. That pulled the cross back from Wednesday's 177.9.
eurjpy.outlook: I lower the range to 175.5–178.0: the yen's role as the AI-selloff hedge and a more hawkish BoJ cap rallies. A close below 175.5 would open 174.
eurjpy.watch: Tokyo comments, Japan wage data, ECB speakers, equity sentiment.

cnhjpy.note: Down about 0.3% to near 23.66 as the yen outpaced a firmer yuan.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did the moving. It gained about 0.5% against the dollar on hawkish BoJ minutes and haven demand, while the yuan rose only about 0.15% after a slightly stronger PBOC fixing at 6.7156. That left the cross in the middle of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.3–23.9 range: Beijing is slowing the yuan and the yen has a haven tailwind, so neither leg should run far.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), Tokyo comments.

watch: Next: US payrolls and Canada jobs (Nov 6), China trade data, TSMC sales (Nov 10), the PBOC's FX reserve hike (Nov 15), the BoE and BSP (Dec 17), plus Tokyo's 159–160 line and foreign flows out of Asian chip stocks.
